technical_requirements: Baseline steady-state: 50k tokens/sec aggregate for batch scoring across two regions (NA/EU)
Concurrency cap: planning for 200 concurrent short requests (avg 32 tokens/request) without p99 > 250ms for single-turn chat
Burst policy: allow transient 2.5x burst for up to 2 minutes per 1-hour window, with rate-limit backpressure and fallback to smaller model
Reserved GPUs: target initial commitment = 8 x H100-equivalent (can be mix of q8 quantized variants), with scale-to-zero disabled for reserved pool
Latency SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 250ms for short-sequence workloads (<=64 tokens); tail mitigation required (profiling + KV cache warmup)
Failover: automatic routing to lower-capacity hosted nodes acceptable for non-sensitive traffic; no hosted fallback for EU-regulated datasets
Observability: token-level cost metrics, per-model latency histograms, and per-route tracing required for first 12 months
negotiation_points: Define 'min tokens/sec' in contract: Maranth requests guaranteed steady-state tokens/sec per-region with credits/refunds for underperformance
Precise concurrency accounting: how concurrency is measured (API connection vs active KV cache entries) — need alignment
Burst rules: exact algorithm for burst replenishment, metrics used to trigger throttling, and grace periods
GPU equivalence: what Redwood counts as 'H100-equivalent' for pricing and guarantees (fp16 vs q8 perf factors)
Credits/penalties: proposed SLA credit ladder for sustained degradation beyond 5% of target over 1 hour
Migration window: lead time for adding reserved GPUs vs immediate burst — want 7-day guaranteed provisioning for extra capacity or pre-booked bursts
Data residency enforcement: contractual clause for EU-only inference nodes and audit rights
